description: Call processing for about 1.15 million voice lines (copper and interconnected VoIP), including delivery of 911 calls to NG911 system service providers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Public safety: 911 calls must complete; PSAP notice within 30 minutes and NORS notification within 120 minutes of discovering a qualifying outage (47 CFR 4.9(f), (h)); RPO is the age of the last archived element configuration (archive on every change)
manual_workaround: Fail VoIP to the geo-redundant SBC cluster; reroute trunks through the second IMS site; TDM switches keep running if the management plane is lost
dependent_third_parties: NG911 system service providers; SS7 interconnect partners; voice core equipment vendors
dependent_people_or_facilities: NOC-1 and NOC-2; central office technicians; 410 central offices
quantified_impact_basis: Voice revenue and usage (about $1.2 million a day) plus SLA credits to 1,900 enterprise accounts and incremental care and field costs; public safety impact dominates
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 run their own softswitches and SBCs (two AQ-02 SBC clusters past vendor support)
single_points_of_failure: Two IMS core sites; 911 trunk groups per NG911 provider

description: Internet access for about 2.6 million subscribers over fiber and DSL, including DNS and DHCP
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Revenue and churn (consumer broadband is about $6.3 million a day); customers depend on broadband for work, school, and VoIP calling to 911; outage-related call surges overload care
manual_workaround: Reroute around failed transport; restore element configurations from the archive; status page and outage messages in IVR and chatbot
dependent_third_parties: Internet transit and peering providers; optical and access equipment vendors
quantified_impact_basis: One day of consumer broadband revenue in credits (about $6.3 million) plus about $1.4 million care surge and overtime and an estimated $1.7 million churn effect
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 access networks are managed from their own flat management networks
single_points_of_failure: Regional broadband network gateways in each state

business_process: Network surveillance, outage response, and regulatory outage reporting
description: 24x7 NOC monitoring, fault isolation, dispatch, PSAP and 988 notifications, NORS and DIRS filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The 30-minute PSAP clock and the 120-minute NORS clock run from discovery; without surveillance, outages are found late and clocks are missed
manual_workaround: NOC-2 takes over surveillance; manual PSAP call tree from the printed contact binder; NORS filed from a standalone workstation
quantified_impact_basis: Longer outages and SLA penalties across all services (estimated 10% extension of outage time) plus regulatory exposure for missed notices
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 alarms reach the NOC through a manual bridge
single_points_of_failure: Single surveillance tool instance (active-passive across NOC-1 and NOC-2)

description: Dedicated Ethernet, wavelengths, and private networks for 110,000 business accounts, including 1,900 enterprise and government accounts and about 140 federal agency circuits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract SLAs (most at 99.95% monthly availability, about 22 minutes a month); federal and enterprise contracts carry credits and termination rights
manual_workaround: Protected paths reroute automatically; manual reroute by the NOC for unprotected circuits
dependent_third_parties: Long-haul fiber partners; optical equipment vendors
quantified_impact_basis: Business revenue of about $4.0 million a day exposed to SLA credits (assume 60%) plus expedite costs and termination risk on large contracts
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-03 transport rings join the backbone at two points
single_points_of_failure: Two backbone routes into the Carolinas

business_process: Wholesale backhaul and SS7 signaling transport
description: Wireless backhaul, wholesale transport for 64 carrier customers, and SS7 signaling transport for 14 small rural carriers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Other carriers' customers lose service (including their 911 calling); SS7 outages are reportable by the company as an SS7 provider (47 CFR 4.9(d)); wholesale SLAs
manual_workaround: STP pairs fail over; protected backhaul rings; manual reroute
quantified_impact_basis: Wholesale revenue of about $1.2 million a day in SLA credits plus SS7 customer credits and expedite costs
single_points_of_failure: One STP pair per mated region (two regions)

description: Provisioning and delivery of court-ordered intercepts and call-identifying information to law enforcement
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Court orders must be implemented promptly and securely; a failed or compromised intercept must be reported to the affected agencies (47 CFR 1.20003(c)); public safety and national security impact
manual_workaround: Re-provision active orders from the mediation platform's order records; trusted third party fallback for delivery
dependent_third_parties: CALEA trusted third party; intercept equipment vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director, Lawful Intercept Compliance; about 30 authorized employees
quantified_impact_basis: Low direct cost; impact is regulatory, legal, and to public safety
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 intercepts run on their legacy platforms and SSI plans
single_points_of_failure: Two mediation nodes in one isolated enclave per data center

description: Phone, chat, and retail care for about 3 million accounts (about 3.1 million contacts a month), 35% handled by three outsourced care vendors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outages create call surges; agents must authenticate callers before discussing call detail (47 CFR 64.2010(b)); care cannot run without the BSS for more than one shift
manual_workaround: Offline account report for outage messaging; callback queue; IVR outage messages; send call detail only to the address of record
dependent_third_parties: CCaaS vendor; care vendors CV-1 to CV-3; chatbot vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 1,700 in-house agents; about 2,600 vendor agents; 3 in-house care centers
quantified_impact_basis: Agent idle time, repeat contacts, and abandoned sales (about 3% of daily revenue) plus surge staffing
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 customers are served from their legacy billing systems
single_points_of_failure: Single BSS instance; single CCaaS tenant

business_process: Managed network services for business customers (SL-1)
description: Managed SD-WAN, managed firewall, and managed Wi-Fi for about 3,400 business customers, operated from the managed services portal and orchestration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer contracts promise 4-hour restoration and change service levels; customers rely on the service for their own security controls (P09)
manual_workaround: Customer devices keep forwarding with the last configuration; manual changes through break-glass access
dependent_third_parties: SD-WAN and firewall equipment vendors' cloud controllers
quantified_impact_basis: SL-1 revenue of about $0.9 million a day exposed to credits plus customer escalation and termination risk
single_points_of_failure: Vendor cloud controllers for SD-WAN orchestration

business_process: Hosted unified communications and contact center (SL-2)
description: Cloud voice, collaboration, and contact center seats for about 1,250 business customers (about 96,000 seats), including their customers' 911 calls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers lose phones and their contact centers at once; 911 calling from hosted seats; interconnected VoIP outage reporting (47 CFR 4.9(g)); recordings are customer confidential data
manual_workaround: Failover to the second Cloud B region; call forwarding to mobile numbers
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; telephone number and messaging partners
quantified_impact_basis: SL-2 revenue of about $0.6 million a day in credits plus customer contact center losses passed through as claims
single_points_of_failure: Interconnect SBC pair for Cloud B traffic

description: Order management, design, activation, and number porting for new and changed services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Installs can be rescheduled; backlog grows by about 9,000 orders a day
manual_workaround: Manual work orders; activation from element managers by engineers
quantified_impact_basis: Deferred installation revenue and rescheduling costs
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 orders run on their legacy systems

description: Dispatch and work management for about 4,800 field technicians
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Storm restoration depends on dispatch; repair commitments to business customers
manual_workaround: Paper tickets; phone dispatch from regional garages

business_process: Usage mediation, rating, billing, and collections
description: CDR collection and rating, bill runs, payments, and collections for about 2.7 million accounts on the converged BSS
process_owner: Vice President, Billing and Revenue Assurance
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Switches buffer CDRs for 72 hours; past that, toll records and the CPNI record customers can dispute are lost; bill cycles can slip a few days
manual_workaround: Hold bill runs; switch CDR buffers; estimated billing only with approval
quantified_impact_basis: Cash deferral of about $0.6 million a day of collections (recovered later) and rework
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 and AQ-03 bill on legacy systems

description: Online account access, bill pay, and the customer-service chatbot (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Online CPNI access must stay authenticated under 64.2010(c); loss of the portal shifts contacts to phone care
manual_workaround: Phone channel; status page; chatbot in outage-message mode
quantified_impact_basis: Lost call deflection (about 70,000 extra calls a day) and delayed payments
acquired_carrier_dependency: AQ-02 portal is separate (password reset gap, POAM-006)
AQ-03 payroll still on the seller provider under a transition agreement

description: Monthly and quarterly close, 10-Q and 10-K preparation, and Form 8-K support
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; during quarter-end close the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Manual journals; extend close by up to 2 days
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time and external audit cost; regulatory and reputation impact if a filing is late

business_process: Operations at AQ-02 and AQ-03 (legacy billing, care, and network management)
description: Billing, care, and network management for about 237,000 acquired accounts until migration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same public safety and care drivers as BP-01 and BP-07 for the acquired territories; legacy systems back up nightly, so the real RPO is 24 hours against a 15-minute target
manual_workaround: Paper tickets; enterprise NOC bridge; enterprise care agents read legacy screens
dependent_systems: AQ-02 and AQ-03 legacy billing, directories, management networks
dependent_third_parties: Legacy billing vendors; legacy managed IT provider at AQ-03
quantified_impact_basis: Acquired-territory revenue (about $0.7 million a day) plus credits and care costs
single_points_of_failure: Single legacy billing instance per carrier; untested restores

business_process: Regulatory filings and lawful process response
description: CPNI certifications, CALEA filings, NORS final reports, subpoena and court order responses
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Filing deadlines are days to weeks, not hours (for example, the NORS final report within 30 days)
manual_workaround: Prepare filings from document repositories offline
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time; late filing exposure only if the outage exceeds several days
